title: Is it okay to deceive audience?
author: FreeQ1337
selftext:
When I look at ebbtide or even more at defilade it is obvious it is vibecoded, yet none of these disclose AI use.

Should we all just drop it and not give a shit ?

comments.author: dtlater
comments.body: No

replies.author: FreeQ1337
replies.body: Uhh so you say we should disclose it?

replies.author: dtlater
replies.body:
Not proactively, but if a distribution platform has a question about whether AI was used for a specific purpose, and you used it for that purpose, then trying to trick people is dishonest.

I also agree with yes guy, that the product should be able to stand on its own merits and it's lame to judge by creation methods, but that's a separate topic from what you asked.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
Yes.

A product should stand on it's merits, not its creation tools.

Be well.

replies.author: FreeQ1337
replies.body: Agree.

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body: Just consider that you could open yourself up to lawsuits if it goes well, basically dooming the product regardless. Players will scrutinize if a product gains even a little bit of attention.

replies.author: Pokeperson5
replies.body: What law would even be broken lol?

replies.author: dtlater
replies.body: I'm guessing this was originally just "Yes" because mine was just "No" and that's kinda funny, but I don't think this makes a case for why it's good to deceive your audience

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body:
It’s an answer to the OP's question: "Should we all drop it?"

Not disclosing tools isn't inherently deception. The end product either stands on its merits or it doesn't. After 40+ years in software engineering and traditional art, policing creation tools has always been a pointless distraction from whether the work itself is actually good.

replies.author: dtlater
replies.body: 100% agree that we should drop it. Every serious dev on earth is using AI assistance, and they way we have to annotate whether we used it "appropriately" is arbitrary.

comments.author: GKR990
comments.body: I don't think it is deceptive. I think it is respectful of your audience to disclose it, but you don't owe them any kind of disclosure.

comments.author: happinessMachiine
comments.body: If people don't disclose that they made their game with AI, it will destroy the indie game industry. People will just stick to the games they loved from a few years ago, and/or go outside. Put the label on your game.

replies.author: FreeQ1337
replies.body: I think it will

replies.author: First-Tutor-5454
replies.body: no

comments.author: BuildAnything4
comments.body:
I wouldn't lie to a paying customer, but I dont publish on steam either.

Steam has set up a double standard where you only need to declare AI if you used it for assets though.  So they've essentially incentivised game developers to hide AI use to get around the declaration.

replies.author: frigginwizard420
replies.body:
I've already seen people trying to loophole that so much. 
They seem to think that if they tell Claude to make the assets by writing draw code to generate the assets with game code, then it's code and not art and they don't need to disclose

replies.author: BuildAnything4
replies.body: Yeah, exactly.  It's fine if there's a category for purists who want completely human made games, but trying to draw distinctions about what kind of ai use is ok and what isn't is nonsense.

replies.author: Count_JohnnyJ
replies.body: To be frank, they are being truthful when they generate assets with code and then say they only used AI for code. The situation is one of many that highlights how dumb steam's ai disclosure policy is. It just needs to be all or nothing.

replies.author: Hefty-Reaction-3028
replies.body:
I think that actually is materially different from using an image model directly

It does not involve taking in art as training data the way that image models do

Edit: well if it's a multimodal model it will have been trained with images ig

replies.author: No-Bee-231
replies.body: CODE IS ART

replies.author: viral-architect
replies.body: We accept terms and conditions constantly that literally rob us of our right to our own property but we have a problem if AI was used.

comments.author: Asleep_Stage_451
comments.body: I used a phone to type this.

replies.author: NoHurry28
replies.body: I downvote ALL phoneslop.  Phoneslop is ruining the world by stealing engagement from traditional mouse and keyboard users

comments.author: frindenolms
comments.body: Hahahahahahaha yes. and you're not even deceiving the audience in the 1st place becuz its a game how r you deceiving them? by not disclosing it?

replies.author: frindenolms
replies.body: eminem didn't even disclose his music video as ai-assisted even tho he ai-generated his young slim shady and its vocals

comments.author: HaphazardlyOrganized
comments.body:
No, just on principle. Deceiving the audience is a breach of trust and the worry of being "discovered" will eat at you. 

Respect your audience

replies.author: Hefty-Reaction-3028
replies.body:
Lying would be deceptive

Not disclosing is not deceptive unless it's breaking some platform rule

replies.author: HaphazardlyOrganized
replies.body:
Op's question was literally about "deceiving" 

And lies my ommission are still lies

replies.author: Hefty-Reaction-3028
replies.body:
>about deceiving

The OP is written in a way that implies that not disclosing itself is a lie

>lies by omission

But it's not a lie by omission. Nobody should be assuming either way.

It's only a lie by omission if you're doing something that would suggest that the lie claim is not true, like post it on a platform that *REQUIRES* disclosure and not doing it.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
This.

Just because others are lowering their standards doesn't mean we should be doing that too.

If you encounter people who are vehemently anti-ai, accept that they weren't your audience to begin with, focus on the ones who enjoy your game, and respect your audience enough not to lie to them or hide things like this from them.

replies.author: Ok_Tea_8763
replies.body: Yeah, but: I do not need them to trust me, I just need them to buy my game.

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body:
On the one hand, I think a tool shouldn't matter. On the other, the mountain of junk that is being made with AI is so big that every game without a large marketing budget will simply die. Quality games, whether or not they are made with AI, won't gain any attention. They simply won't be seen, discovered, unless you have a load of followers or deep pockets.


I wish we had better ways of sifting all the crap from the few good gems.

replies.author: greentrillion
replies.body: What "quality" games have you seen made made with AI?

replies.author: Count_JohnnyJ
replies.body: Every AAA game in the last 12 months used AI in some undisclosed capacity. Fortnite uses it at nearly every level of development and that game is more popular than ever.

replies.author: Bottlefistfucker
replies.body: It was like this before. Whats mindblowing to me is all these dilusional people puking crap onto the storefront and throwing away 100$

replies.author: Own_Badger6076
replies.body: Something to consider is actually supporting games you make long term. If you just want to pump out one and done chump change then you're a slop merchant - games that receive long term dev support grow communities around them and gain in popularity.  If you're expecting to be an overnight smash hit, you're in the wrong field.

replies.author: greentrillion
replies.body: What "quality" games without a large marketing budget have you seen made made with AI?

replies.author: OnyxMonolith
replies.body: I think i can name 1 that has financial success but wouldn’t call it quality

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body: No, you should not deceive your fans and customers. It's unethical, and a poor business practice for indies in particular - as an indie, you'll likely depend on the support from communities that are excited about your projects as you get going.

comments.author: throwaway09234023322
comments.body: Yeah, that's fine. The antis are fanatics and I won't disclose it just to piss them off.

comments.author: kujasgoldmine
comments.body: A lot of paople are saying "Little bit of ai was used", when in truth it was almost all, if not all was vibe coded. I've seen people first admit full AI usage in steam disclosure and then editing it a few days later to be just optimizations and translations.

comments.author: FervantFlea
comments.body: FWIW, both those games have a detailed AI disclosure in the correct spot on Steam, so not sure your premise is correct.

comments.author: FailedGradAdmissions
comments.body:
Morals aside, it’s still fraud. Legally as simple as that if someone would not had purchased your product if they had known XYZ about you or your product it is fraud. Nothing has to be wrong with the product. A textbook example is you sell a house where someone had been murdered, didn’t tell the buyer and they wouldn’t had bought it if they knew.

Would someone sue you for deceiving with a $5 game, probably not. But it could happen and they would win in court, same principle.

A bigger risk is if and when people do eventually find out  they will go nuclear.

BTW, Ebbtide does have an AI disclosure in their Steam page, defilade doesn’t while looking even more vibe coded.

Just be honest, make a good game and price it highly enough haters don’t even buy your game.

replies.author: DrBimboo
replies.body:
I dont care. People are dumb sheeps and I dont want them to boycot and review bomb me.

If you ask me, not a single line of code ever touched visual studio, Ive written it all on notepad on  Windows XP.

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body: why are you convinced ebbtide is vibecoded? Doesn't look like it at all to me.

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body: nah. They're talkign about the specific deception of not disclosing that you used AI dev assist. Which doesn't require disclosure according to the policy, and very obviously isn't fraud.

replies.author: Hefty-Reaction-3028
replies.body: That's obviously not deception either, unless they claimed that it was not made with AI

comments.author: MilaKunisWatermelon
comments.body: If the backlash you get for using AI is just as bad as the backlash you get for being found to not disclose using AI, then there is no incentive to disclose using AI.

comments.author: MilaKunisWatermelon
comments.body:
Not disclosing AI use is not the same as lying about AI use.

Ya’ll act like we should have a special arm band that people who use AI should have to wear.

comments.author: Hefty-Reaction-3028
comments.body: That's not dishonest. Lying is dishonest. Using AI without disclosure is not a lie. If someone assumes something about my game, that's on them.

comments.author: Garland_Key
comments.body: I will die on this hill. It is none of their business how you created something. By self reporting, you are only feeding the legitimatacy of the witch hunt.

comments.author: NeusomaDev
comments.body:
It's not okay to deceive your audience.

It definitely is annoying to know that huge publishers flagrantly ignore disclosure requirements because they make the calculated choice to deceive the audience to improve their revenue. And it's also annoying to know that the witch hunt brigade on this subject is just a bunch of Internet crybullies that target smaller indie developers because they can't touch the big publishers.

But as annoying as those things are, they don't rationalize or justify deceiving your audience, no.

comments.author: Guy_LeFevre
comments.body: Absolutely not.

comments.author: Evening_Till_3779
comments.body: Ebbtide does disclose AI use, not sure what you're talking about.

comments.author: MastaFoo69
comments.body: No.

comments.author: fued
comments.body: those games are gonna get roasted when they released, they are way too obviously ai vibed

comments.author: Ok_Tea_8763
comments.body: Not just ok, it's almost mandatory at this point. Players will have to get used to AI in their games.

comments.author: beta_1457
comments.body:
On Ebbtide's Steam page it says this:

>  
AI Generated Content Disclosure

>The developers describe how their game uses AI Generated Content like this:

>*Generative AI was used during development to create the soundtrack, some prerecorded voices, sound effects, ambient audio and event illustrations, and to create or refine selected 3D models. AI-assisted tools were also used to translate in-game text. All AI-generated content was reviewed and edited by the developer before inclusion. The game does not generate content with AI during gameplay.*

  
So I don't think they are hiding anything.

comments.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
comments.body: This post is not specific to AI based game development. See rule #1.
